# Boring Linux: Master Reference Architecture {.unnumbered}

> **Reference platform:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS ("Resolute Raccoon") & Linux Kernel 7.0.
> **Scope:** 16 Modules across 5 Parts covering Silicon Architecture, Kernel Internals, High-Performance/AI Infrastructure, and Cloud-Native Engineering.
> **Baseline:** Linux 7.0 (pure cgroup v2, Maple Tree, MGLRU, PREEMPT_RT, eBPF CO-RE), oxidized userspace (`rust-coreutils`, `sudo-rs`, `ntpd-rs`, Glibc 2.43), systemd v258+ with Varlink and run0, and OpenSSH 10.2 hybrid Post-Quantum cryptography.

```text
Boring Linux Master Architecture
├── Part I: Silicon & Kernel Internals
│   ├── 01. Hardware Architecture & Modern Userspace
│   ├── 02. Kernel Internals: Core, Scheduling & Locking
│   ├── 03. Kernel Internals: Memory, VFS & I/O
│   └── 04. Kernel Internals: Isolation, Security & eBPF
├── Part II: Systems Engineering & Host Infrastructure
│   ├── 05. Systems Programming & Automation (Go & Rust)
│   ├── 06. Systems Administration & Immutable Linux
│   └── 07. Storage, Filesystems & Encryption
├── Part III: Networking, Security & High-Performance AI
│   ├── 08. Network Engineering & Software-Defined Networking
│   ├── 09. Security, Cryptography & Compliance
│   └── 10. High-Performance, Real-Time & AI Infrastructure
├── Part IV: Virtualization, Containers & Platform Engineering
│   ├── 11. Virtualization & Private Cloud
│   ├── 12. Containers & Kubernetes Orchestration
│   └── 13. DevOps, IaC & Platform Engineering
└── Part V: Observability, GitOps & Production Blueprints
    ├── 14. Observability, SRE & Performance Engineering
    ├── 15. GitOps & Cloud-Native Control Planes
    └── 16. Appendices, Runbooks & Reference Blueprints
```

## Architectural Principles

Every conceptual chapter in this book adheres to a disciplined engineering standard:
1. **First-Principles Mental Model**: Visual architecture diagrams showing hardware interfaces, ring transitions, or packet pathways.
2. **Under the Hood (Kernel / Source Reference)**: Kernel structures, syscall definitions, `/proc` and `/sys` knobs.
3. **Production Configuration & CLI Craft**: Copy-pasteable, idempotent commands and system configurations.
4. **Verification & Observability**: How to prove subsystem execution using `bpftool`, `perf`, `rtla`, and runtime probes.
5. **Common Pitfalls & Traps**: Production failure modes, race conditions, and architectural misconfigurations.

Every module culminates in a dedicated **Workbook** providing declarative bootstrap scripts (Incus/KVM), 3 guided build labs, and 3 break/fix chaos engineering scenarios.
